chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: Billy Shaw's Gale days and the first small band
summary: Cobb sorts out when Billy Shaw worked for Gale, says he worked seven months until January 1948, and lists his five-piece rhythm section with Dave Page and later Booty Wood.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Arnett, you said -- did you mention Billy Shaw in that connection?
Yeah, he was working for Gale Agency then.
When was he working for them? Oh, you mean his son?
No, Billy himself was in Gale Agency. He didn't have Shaw Agency then.
Didn't he?
He had Shaw Agency later. I'm speaking of 1947 now. He was working for Gale.
Oh, I didn't know that.
His secretary was Billy ie Miller.
Oh, I didn't know about that.
So I went in the hospital after seven months of working on that operation, and they didn't send me a penny postcard.
But wait a minute. Were you working with this band for seven months?

Well, seven months until I had to take down and really have the operation. I -- let me see now. From -- I started to work in April that year and worked on with the bookings I had and had to take down January of the
next year, which was '48.
Well, when you went in this Baby Grand played in the band, it was just you and Dave Page and the rhythm section, was it?
Rhythm section and Dave Page and myself, just two horns, five pieces.
Who'd you have on rhythm then?
I had Butch Ballard on drums, George Rhodes on piano and Poor Jumpin' George Jones on -- I mean Walter Buchanan on bass. Poor George came in later.
Well, when you did go (inaudible)? did add Bootsy Wood and...

I added Bootsy in -- I went into the Philadelphia situation, and it was down the line I added it on. During the SEVEN months I thought I would enlarge my band and I added Bootsy, and maybe it was three months later.
I see.
But on the beginning I just went in for two weeks. That's why I had just five pieces, see.
But by the time you'd make these Apollo records for Parlor, you'd got Bootsy, hadn't you?
What?
By the time you made the records for Apollo for Parlor --
I had Bootsy.
You had Bootsy by then.
Yeah, see, I added him on a little later, but he didn't work at the Baby Grand with me.
